content.intro: {state} charges a {stateRate} excise tax and a separate vehicle sales tax when ownership changes, then a yearly registration fee that falls as the vehicle gets older.

howItWorks.text: The excise tax is figured on the purchase price. The state vehicle sales tax is figured on the same price.
A trade-in does not lower the price either tax is figured on.
Registration is paid every year. The fee depends on how many years the vehicle has been registered, and drops in steps of four years.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the tax in {state}?
faq.text: No. Service Oklahoma tells clerks not to subtract the trade-in from the purchase price, so both the excise tax and the vehicle sales tax are charged on the full price.

faq.q: Is there local sales tax on a vehicle in {state}?
faq.text: Service Oklahoma's procedure lists only the state excise tax and the state vehicle sales tax on a purchase.
